1.title: Three Major Fungal Diseases
1.html:
• Powdery mildew (oïdium): whitening appears on the shoots and berry surfaces, and the berries gradually burst as they grow
  • Downy mildew (mildiou): causes severe damage to the bunches, drying them out completely; damage to the leaves reduces the efficiency of photosynthesis
  • Grey rot (pourriture grise): the berry surface is covered with a grey powdery layer; larvae of the grape moths that bore into the skin speed the spread of grey rot
2.title: Pheromone Mating Disruption: A Model of Ecological Control
2.html:
There are more and more ecological methods of fighting these pests and diseases, the most representative being "pheromone mating disruption" (confusion sexuelle): capsules releasing female moth pheromones are hung in the vineyard, luring the males into losing their way and failing to find real mates.

The result: mating is greatly restricted and the risk of grey rot is cut by up to half — greatly reducing the need for insecticides, an important part of sustainable viticulture in Alsace.
3.title: Ripeness Monitoring and Harvest
3.html:
Ripening begins in mid-August (véraison), when the skins start to take on their final colour, a process lasting about 45 days — during which the sugar in the fruit keeps rising and acidity gradually falls. In mid-September the leaves remaining around the bunches are removed to let sunlight fall directly on them, lowering the risk of grey rot.

Harvest usually begins 100 days after flowering, with the official opening date announced by the "Alsace wine expert committee". To this day the great majority of harvesting is still done by hand — about 250 working hours per hectare, which works out to more than 30 pickers working at once to bring in one hectare in a day.
4.question: How does the ecological technique of "pheromone mating disruption" (confusion sexuelle) lower the risk of grey rot?
4.options.0: It kills the grape moth larvae directly
4.options.1: It releases female moth pheromones that make males lose their way and fail to mate, reducing the number of larvae and cutting the risk of grey rot by up to half
4.options.2: It plants pest-repellent plants around the vineyard
4.explanation: Pheromone mating disruption hangs capsules releasing female moth pheromones in the vineyard, luring males into losing their way and failing to find real mates, which greatly limits mating success — since the larvae of grape moths boring into the skin speed the spread of grey rot, reducing their numbers cuts the risk of grey rot by up to half, while also greatly reducing insecticide use.
